'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''

***At least 14 people are killed and at least 15 others are injured in an [[Israel]]i airstrike on a residential building in [[Ain Yaaqoub]], [[Akkar Governorate]], [[North Lebanon|Northern Lebanon]]. *[[Ecuadorian security crisis]]
**[[November 2024 Guayaquil prison riot]]
***Seventeen people are killed and 15 more injured after a [[prison riot]] at the [[Litoral Penitentiary]] in [[Guayaquil]], [[Ecuador]]. [https://apnews.com/article/ecuador-noboa-prison-killings-gangs-drug-cartels-41b7062a5a731c71bfce4897735f70e1 (AP)]
*[[Haitian crisis (2018–present)|Haitian crisis]]
**The [[U.S.]] [[Federal Aviation Administration]] issues a temporary 30-day ground on all [[List of airlines of the United States|U.S. airlines]] from flying to [[Haiti]] after [[Gang war in Haiti|gangs]] shot at a [[Spirit Airlines]] aircraft that was attempting to land at [[Toussaint Louverture International Airport]] in [[Port-au-Prince]], Haiti, yesterday. The airport is also closed indefinitely in response to the shooting. [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/nation-world/world/article295444429.html (''Miami Herald'')]  [https://www.scrippsnews.com/world/faa-grounds-us-flights-to-haiti-after-gunfire-strikes-spirit-airlines-aircraft (Scripps News)]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[The Pentagon]] reports that several [[missile]]s and [[drone warfare|drones]] launched at the {{ship|USS|Spruance|DDG-111|6}} and the {{ship|USS|Stockdale|DDG-106|6}} by the [[Houthis]] are shot down. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1knpnlp1leo (BBC)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab militants]] ambush and kill two [[South West State]] soldiers who were travelling on [[motorcycle]]s on the highway between [[Wanlaweyn]] and [[Afgooye]] in [[Lower Shabelle]], [[Somalia]]. [https://www.hiiraan.com/news4/2024/Nov/198891/al_shabab_ambush_kills_two_southwest_state_soldiers_in_lower_shabelle_region.aspx (Hiiraan Online)]

**The [[United States Department of the Treasury]] sanctions [[Rapid Support Forces]] general [[Abdel Rahman Jumma]], alleging that Jumma is the "primary party" responsible for the [[civilian casualty|violence against civilians]] and [[human rights abuses]] in [[West Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/11/12/us-sanctions-rsf-commander-accused-of-rights-abuses-in-sudans (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture''' 
*[[2024 Booker Prize]]
**English novelist [[Samantha Harvey (author)|Samantha Harvey]] wins the [[Booker Prize]] for her novel ''[[Orbital (novel)|Orbital]]''. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj0jellz4zro (BBC News)]
*Spanish writer [[Álvaro Pombo]] wins the [[Miguel de Cervantes Prize]]. [https://elpais.com/cultura/2024-11-12/el-escritor-espanol-alvaro-pombo-gana-el-premio-cervantes.html (''El País'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Indo-Pakistani smog]]
**The [[Ministry of National Health Services, Regulation and Coordination|Pakistani Health Department]] reports that at least 1.8 million people in [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], [[Pakistan]] have become sick with [[Respiratory disease|respiratory]] and [[eye irritation]] ailments caused by chronic, record-breaking [[air pollution]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-smog-punjab-huge-population-affected-304b37e0e98cf734d40a37a5ec908bd3 (AP)]

**Two people are killed and 12 others are injured in an explosion at a [[food coloring]] factory in [[Louisville]], [[Kentucky]], [[United States]]. [https://www.kcrg.com/2024/11/14/2-employees-killed-workplace-explosion-investigation-into-cause-continues/ (KCRG-TV)] [https://apnews.com/article/louisville-kentucky-explosion-f7293237f0d07e597354505219cfcd09 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse]]
**A [[Juries in the United States|U.S. jury]] awards [[United States dollar|US$]]42 million to three former detainees of the [[Abu Ghraib prison]] in [[Iraq]], thereby holding [[Virginia]]-based military contractor [[CACI]] liable for their role in the torture and mistreatment of the detainees. [https://apnews.com/article/abu-ghraib-civil-trial-iraq-virginia-3a2841ec2892fb111b4e26a70e761208 (AP)]
*[[Anglican Communion sexual abuse cases]]
**[[Justin Welby]], the [[Archbishop of Canterbury]] and the symbolic head of the [[Anglican Communion]], resigns over his handling of [[barrister]] [[John Smyth (barrister)|John Smyth]]'s [[sex abuse]] scandal. [https://www.npr.org/2024/11/12/nx-s1-5188083/archbishop-of-canterbury-justin-welby-resigns-over-sex-abuse-scandal (NPR)] [https://apnews.com/article/justin-welby-resigns-archbishop-of-canterbury-abuse-2ab9cab63572f5062b5a5588698fe492 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections''' 
*[[2024 Mauritian general election]]
**[[Leader of the Opposition (Mauritius)|Opposition leader]] and [[Labour Party (Mauritius)|Labour Party]] candidate [[Navin Ramgoolam]] is elected as [[Prime Minister of Mauritius]], with his coalition [[Alliance du Changement]] winning 60 of the 66 [[National Assembly (Mauritius)|National Assembly]] seats. Former Prime Minister [[Pravind Jugnauth]] resigns following his party's defeat in the election. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/mauritius-opposition-wins-626-votes-election-commission-says-2024-11-12/ (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/11/12/opposition-secures-landslide-victory-in-mauritius-election (Al Jazeera)]
